findings.title: Wrong metric function called on storage error in Create
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`. This means storage failures are recorded under the legacy metric, corrupting both the legacy and storage duration metrics and making it impossible to correctly monitor storage health.

findings.title: Wrong logger placed into context in Delete
findings.body: The code builds `log` with name, kind, and method values on line 96, but then on line 97 inserts `d.Log` (the bare logger without those values) into the context via `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`. This means any downstream code that retrieves the logger from the context will not see the structured fields. It should be `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`.

findings.title: Wrong label value passed as kind in Delete success metric
findings.body: On the success path of Delete, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` (the resource name) as the kind parameter. Every other call in this file passes `options.Kind` for that position. This will produce metric labels with the object name instead of the resource kind, leading to high-cardinality metrics and inconsistency with other operations.

findings.title: Wrong metric function called on storage error in Update
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`. This misattributes storage errors to the legacy metric, the same class of bug as in Create.

findings.title: Wrong metric function called for legacy write in DeleteCollection goroutine
findings.body: Inside the async goroutine that writes to legacy storage, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)`. This means legacy delete-collection durations are recorded as storage durations, corrupting both metrics.

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive context from request context and will be cancelled when the request completes
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection, the goroutines that asynchronously write to legacy storage derive their timeout context from the request context (`ctx`). In Go's HTTP server, the request context is cancelled once the handler returns and the response is written. Since these goroutines are fire-and-forget, the parent request context will typically be cancelled almost immediately after the function returns, causing `context.WithTimeoutCause` to also cancel. This means the legacy writes will likely fail with a context cancellation error before completing, defeating the purpose of the async safety-net write. The goroutines should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (Go 1.21+) or `context.Background()` as the parent.

findings.title: Tests do not verify that legacy storage is actually called asynchronously
findings.body: The mode 3 tests set up mock expectations for legacy Create/Update/Delete but never assert that those mocks were actually called (e.g., via `m.AssertExpectations(t)` or a wait/sleep). Since the legacy writes happen in goroutines, the tests may pass even if the goroutine never executes or panics. This means the core dual-write behavior is not actually verified by the unit tests.
